coverage.main: Read the eighteen-page author-hosted PDF of the IEEE S&P 2019 paper (NESA lab, Zhejiang University): Sections I-VII (attack and defense utility metrics, evaluations, Case Study 1 on transferability, Case Study 2 on defense ensembles), Tables I-IX, and Appendices VIII-XI (model architectures, parameter settings, MNIST supplementary Tables XIV-XVIII). The IEEE Xplore version of record was not accessed.
coverage.supplement: Appendices VIII-XI are embedded in the PDF and read, including the MNIST transferability Table XVII.
coverage.excluded_results: Table III/XIV attack utility (white-box on the original model), defense utility and white-box defense-evaluation tables, detection results, and Case Study 2 (ensembles of defenses attacked with AEs generated on the original model; population and conditioning follow the Section IV setup and are not cross-model transfer rates of the form reported in Case Study 1). ACAC confidence columns are not misclassification outcomes.

result_groups.locator: Section IV-A Evaluation methodology (p. 6); Section V-A (pp. 11-12); Table VIII (CIFAR-10); Appendix XI Table XVII (MNIST)
result_groups.population: 1,000 test examples sampled from those correctly predicted by the original model; AEs from 16 untargeted and targeted attacks; only 'the misclassified AEs generated in Section IV-A' (source-successful; count per attack in the '# of AEs' column) are classified by Models 1-3 (re-initialised copy, slightly different architecture, different architecture)
result_groups.outcome: MR (untargeted: misclassified away from ground truth; targeted: classified as the target class)
result_groups.evidence: The transferred set is explicitly restricted to source-misclassified AEs from source-clean-correct examples (original-model MR is 100.0% in every row, with per-attack AE counts such as 897 or 134). No restriction to examples Models 1-3 classify correctly is stated.

f1.locator: Section IV-A; Section V-A; Appendix VIII-B
f1.evidence: Clean test accuracy of the original (source) models is reported (99.27% MNIST, 85.95% CIFAR-10); Models 1-3 are said to have 'comparable accuracy' without numbers.

f2.evidence: No target-clean-correct restriction or explicit inclusion statement.

f3.evidence: 'we employ the three trained models to classify the misclassified AEs generated in Section IV-A'. Positive conditioning evidence.

f4.evidence: Each row states its AE count (at most 1,000) with one-decimal MR. Ten sampled CIFAR-10 cells (e.g., 88.2% of 897 = 791; 3.7% of 134 = 5) each give a unique count with survey/count_reconstruction.py. Every cell of both tables has not yet been verified, so field 4 stays unclear pending full extraction.

f5.locator: Table VIII Objective column; Appendix IX-A Table XIII
f5.evidence: L-infinity attacks state epsilon (e.g., 0.1/0.2 on CIFAR-10, 0.3/0.5 on MNIST). DeepFool, OM, CW2 and the L0 attacks are minimum-norm or L0 attacks without an L-infinity/L2 radius.

f6.evidence: The official DEEPSEC repository implements attacks, defenses and evaluations and says how to regenerate models, clean samples and AEs. It contains no script or checkpoints for the case-study Models 1-3; not executed.

artifact_checks.result: Listed via the GitHub API (101 files, head 21 May 2019): RawModels/, CleanDatasets/, Attacks/, AdversarialExampleDatasets/ (README only), Defenses/, DefenseEnhancedModels/, Evaluations/ (AttackEvaluations.py, DefenseEvaluations.py, SecurityEvaluation.py). No transferability case-study script or Model 1-3 files located. Not executed.
Author-hosted PDF located by web search and hashed; used because no arXiv version is listed in the corpus.

bounds_checks.reason: Rates are over source-successful AEs from source-clean-correct examples, and target clean accuracies are not printed, so no unconditional bound applies.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Field 4 is a strong reconstruction candidate pending cell-by-cell verification of Tables VIII and XVII.
